newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech FinMin sees budget cuts debate soon-agency.
newsitem.headline: Czech FinMin sees budget cuts debate soon-agency.

text.p: Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik expects the cabinet by early April to discuss his plan to cut almost all 1997 state spending by two percent, the local news agency CTK said on Thursday.
It quoted Kocarnik as saying that the spending cuts, amounting to 11 billion crowns, would exclued social support payments.
"I expect that the government will debate (the proposal) at the end of March or at the beginning of April," CTK quoted Kocarnik as saying.

The Finance Ministry came with plan after the state budget, which was approved as balanced with both revenues and expenditures at 549.1 billion crowns, showed a 6.7 billion crowns deficit at the end of February.
The centre-right government made healthy state finances a cornerstone of its economic policy.
Last year's budget ended with a 1.56 billion deficit, after three years of surpluses.
